messages:
maria: quick heads-up — after yesterday's kernel switch the KV "prefix" cache hit-rate dropped ~15% on canary. saw burst of cold-starts for multi-tenant batch workloads. looking into keying + warmup behavior :thinking:
shaun: can you paste the perf numbers? which models/seq-lens?
eva: ops-bot posted alerts at 09:12, 09:18 for increased token latency and elevated P50.
ops-bot: alert: canary-cluster-42 token-latency P50 increased from 45ms -> 78ms; cache hit-rate down from 82% -> 67% (5m window) 
shaun: thanks. initial profiling shows the kernel change introduced a tiny refactor in the cache key path. old key generation included tenant and route-salt: `key = sha1(tenant_id + "|" + route_salt + "|" + prefix_hash)`
shaun: new code (post-refactor) accidentally builds: `key = sha1(prefix_hash + "|" + route_salt)` — tenant_id omitted in ~0.8% of requests (conditional path for short-prefix fast-path). that explains cross-tenant collisions and lower hit-rate due to noisy eviction. :eyes:
eva: yikes. so collisions caused extra churn and evictions -> more warmups -> higher latency. any PII risk?
security: tagging in — cross-tenant key collisions are a privacy red flag. even if content isn't returned across tenants, metadata could leak via eviction pattern inference. need audit logs for any keys that were shared across tenant ids while this bug was active. also want to know if keys are stored encrypted at rest. :lock:
maria: current KVS is encrypted at rest customer-side for private deployments but not per-key encrypted for hosted. this bug mainly affects hosted canary.
shaun: mitigation options: 1) quick rollback of kernel refactor (safe but expensive), 2) patch keygen to reintroduce tenant_id immediately and backfill, 3) introduce runtime guard: reject fast-path keygen for request with tenant headers missing and fallback to safe path.
eva: ops: can we taint the cache and proactively evict suspect keys from the canary region? that would reduce collision surface without full rollback.
ops-bot: eviction job queued: canary-cluster-42 -> scan and evict keys matching collision-signature (approx). ETA 12 minutes.
shaun: for backfill we can rekey existing entries by re-hashing with tenant_id and copying. simple script: ```python
for k,v in scan(prefixes):
    new_k = sha1(tenant_id + '|' + route_salt + '|' + extract_prefix(k))
    put(new_k, v)
```
shaun: risk: double-write increases storage/temp growth. we should run on a snapshot and rate-limit.
security: please record the copy actions in the audit trail. also rotate route_salt after backfill to prevent replay collisions. we need a TTL for old-key acceptance.
maria: agreed. action items: shaun patch keygen + add unit test preventing any path omitting tenant_id; ops run eviction job and then backfill script on snapshot; security to generate audit report for suspect key matches and recommend route_salt rotation. I'll open a rollback PR if patch isn't green in 30m.
eva: also add a perf regression test that simulates multi-tenant small-prefix workload so the CI flags hit-rate drops >5%.
shaun: making patch now, will post a diff. quick perf note: single-tenant workloads unaffected (hit-rate stable) — this is purely multi-tenant collision amplification.
maria: thanks team. please drop logs/grep patterns here after jobs finish. follow-up sync 10:30 in #eng-runtime if anything odd. :white_check_mark:
